cases.sentence: Иван Васильевич Ломов, сосед Чубукова, здоровый, упитанный, но очень ___.
cases.explain: «мнительный помещик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A drawing-room in CHUBUKOV'S house. [LOMOV enters, wearing a dress-jacket and white gloves. CHUBUKOV rises to meet him.]

cases.sentence: Точно на ___ с визитом!
cases.explain: «Новый год» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Then why are you in evening dress, my precious? As if you're paying a New Year's Eve visit!

cases.sentence: Это было моим ___.
cases.explain: «всегдашним желанием» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. [Interrupting] My dear fellow... I'm so glad, and so on.... Yes, indeed, and all that sort of thing. [Embraces and kisses LOMOV] I've been hoping for it for a long time. It's been my continual desire. [Sheds a tear] And I've always loved you, my angel, as if you were my own son. May God give you both His help and His love and so on, and I did so much hope... What am I behaving in this idiotic way for? I'm off my balance with joy, absolutely off my balance! Oh, with all my soul... I'll go and call Natasha, and all that.

cases.sentence: (Пускает слезу.) И всегда я любил вас, ангел мой, как ___.
cases.explain: «родного сына» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. [Interrupting] My dear fellow... I'm so glad, and so on.... Yes, indeed, and all that sort of thing. [Embraces and kisses LOMOV] I've been hoping for it for a long time. It's been my continual desire. [Sheds a tear] And I've always loved you, my angel, as if you were my own son. May God give you both His help and His love and so on, and I did so much hope... What am I behaving in this idiotic way for? I'm off my balance with joy, absolutely off my balance! Oh, with all my soul... I'll go and call Natasha, and all that.

cases.sentence: Наталья Степановна ___, недурна, образованна… чего ж мне еще нужно?
cases.explain: «отличная хозяйка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. It's cold... I'm trembling all over, just as if I'd got an examination before me. The great thing is, I must have my mind made up. If I give myself time to think, to hesitate, to talk a lot, to look for an ideal, or for real love, then I'll never get married.... Brr!... It's cold! Natalya Stepanovna is an excellent housekeeper, not bad-looking, well-educated.... What more do I want? But I'm getting a noise in my ears from excitement. [Drinks] And it's impossible for me not to marry.... In the first place, I'm already 35--a critical age, so to speak. In the second place, I ought to lead a quiet and regular life.... I suffer from palpitations, I'm excitable and always getting awfully upset.... At this very moment my lips are trembling, and there's a twitch in my right eyebrow.... But the very worst of all is the way I sleep. I no sooner get into bed and begin to go off when suddenly something in my left side--gives a pull, and I can feel it in my shoulder and head.... I jump up like a lunatic, walk about a bit, and lie down again, but as soon as I begin to get off to sleep there's another pull! And this may happen twenty times....

cases.sentence: У меня порок сердца, ___, я вспыльчив и всегда ужасно волнуюсь…
cases.explain: «постоянные сердцебиения» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. It's cold... I'm trembling all over, just as if I'd got an examination before me. The great thing is, I must have my mind made up. If I give myself time to think, to hesitate, to talk a lot, to look for an ideal, or for real love, then I'll never get married.... Brr!... It's cold! Natalya Stepanovna is an excellent housekeeper, not bad-looking, well-educated.... What more do I want? But I'm getting a noise in my ears from excitement. [Drinks] And it's impossible for me not to marry.... In the first place, I'm already 35--a critical age, so to speak. In the second place, I ought to lead a quiet and regular life.... I suffer from palpitations, I'm excitable and always getting awfully upset.... At this very moment my lips are trembling, and there's a twitch in my right eyebrow.... But the very worst of all is the way I sleep. I no sooner get into bed and begin to go off when suddenly something in my left side--gives a pull, and I can feel it in my shoulder and head.... I jump up like a lunatic, walk about a bit, and lie down again, but as soon as I begin to get off to sleep there's another pull! And this may happen twenty times....

cases.sentence: Вам, уважаемая Наталья Степановна, известно, что я давно уже, с ___, имею честь знать ваше семейство.
cases.explain: «самого детства» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: LOMOV. I shall try to be brief. You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother. The Lomovs and the Chubukovs have always had the most friendly, and I might almost say the most affectionate, regard for each other. And, as you know, my land is a near neighbour of yours. You will remember that my Oxen Meadows touch your birchwoods.

cases.sentence: Моя покойная тетушка и ее супруг, от которых я, как вы изволите знать, получил в наследство землю, всегда относились с ___ к вашему батюшке и к покойной матушке.
cases.explain: «глубоким уважением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: LOMOV. I shall try to be brief. You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother. The Lomovs and the Chubukovs have always had the most friendly, and I might almost say the most affectionate, regard for each other. And, as you know, my land is a near neighbour of yours. You will remember that my Oxen Meadows touch your birchwoods.

cases.sentence: Моя покойная тетушка и ее супруг, от которых я, как вы изволите знать, получил в наследство землю, всегда относились с глубоким уважением к вашему батюшке и к ___.
cases.explain: «покойной матушке» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: LOMOV. I shall try to be brief. You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother. The Lomovs and the Chubukovs have always had the most friendly, and I might almost say the most affectionate, regard for each other. And, as you know, my land is a near neighbour of yours. You will remember that my Oxen Meadows touch your birchwoods.

cases.sentence: Род Ломовых и род Чубуковых всегда находились в самых дружественных и, можно даже сказать, ___.
cases.explain: «родственных отношениях» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: LOMOV. I shall try to be brief. You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother. The Lomovs and the Chubukovs have always had the most friendly, and I might almost say the most affectionate, regard for each other. And, as you know, my land is a near neighbour of yours. You will remember that my Oxen Meadows touch your birchwoods.

cases.sentence: И мой дедушка, и прадедушка считали, что ___ доходила до Горелого болота — значит, Воловьи Лужки были наши.
cases.explain: «ихняя земля» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. No, it isn't at all like that! Both my grandfather and great-grandfather reckoned that their land extended to Burnt Marsh--which means that Oxen Meadows were ours. I don't see what there is to argue about. It's simply silly!

cases.sentence: И мой дедушка, и прадедушка считали, что ихняя земля доходила до ___ — значит, Воловьи Лужки были наши.
cases.explain: «Горелого болота» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. No, it isn't at all like that! Both my grandfather and great-grandfather reckoned that their land extended to Burnt Marsh--which means that Oxen Meadows were ours. I don't see what there is to argue about. It's simply silly!

cases.sentence: До сих пор мы вас считали ___, другом, в прошлом году давали вам свою молотилку, и через это самим нам пришлось домолачивать свой хлеб в ноябре, а вы поступаете с нами, как с цыганами.
cases.explain: «хорошим соседом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. I can make you a present of them myself, because they're mine! Your behaviour, Ivan Vassilevitch, is strange, to say the least! Up to this we have always thought of you as a good neighbour, a friend: last year we lent you our threshing-machine, although on that account we had to put off our own threshing till November, but you behave to us as if we were gipsies. Giving me my own land, indeed! No, really, that's not at all neighbourly! In my opinion, it's even impudent, if you want to know....

cases.sentence: Сударыня, никогда я ___ не захватывал и обвинять меня в этом никому не позволю…
cases.explain: «чужих земель» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: LOMOV. Then you make out that I'm a land-grabber? Madam, never in my life have I grabbed anybody else's land, and I shan't allow anybody to accuse me of having done so.... [Quickly steps to the carafe and drinks more water] Oxen Meadows are mine!

cases.sentence: Вот именно, ___, я не привык, чтобы со мною разговаривали таким тоном и прочее.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. You may take it that I know whether I have the right or not. Because, young man, I'm not used to being spoken to in that tone of voice, and so on: I, young man, am twice your age, and ask you to speak to me without agitating yourself, and all that.

cases.sentence: Я, ___, старше вас вдвое и прошу вас говорить со мною без ажитации и тому подобное.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. You may take it that I know whether I have the right or not. Because, young man, I'm not used to being spoken to in that tone of voice, and so on: I, young man, am twice your age, and ask you to speak to me without agitating yourself, and all that.

cases.sentence: Так ___ не поступают, Степан Степаныч!
cases.explain: «хорошие соседи» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. No, you just think I'm a fool and want to have me on! You call my land yours, and then you want me to talk to you calmly and politely! Good neighbours don't behave like that, Stepan Stepanitch! You're not a neighbour, you're a grabber!

cases.sentence: Можете подавать в суд, ___, и тому подобное!
cases.explain: «милостивый государь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. To court? You can take it to court, and all that! You can! I know you; you're just on the look-out for a chance to go to court, and all that.... You pettifogger! All your people were like that! All of them!

cases.sentence: Вот и верь после этого ___!
cases.explain: «добрым соседям» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. What a rascal! What trust can one have in one's neighbours after that!

cases.sentence: И эта кикимора, эта, вот именно, ___ осмеливается еще делать предложение и прочее!
cases.explain: «куриная слепота» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. And that blind hen, yes, that turnip-ghost has the confounded cheek to make a proposal, and so on! What? A proposal!

cases.sentence: Я теперь припоминаю: Воловьи Лужки в ___ ваши.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. Forgive us, Ivan Vassilevitch, we were all a little heated.... I remember now: Oxen Meadows really are yours.

cases.sentence: Должно быть, вывихнул или ___ покусали…
cases.explain: «другие собаки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. I don't know.... Must have got twisted, or bitten by some other dog.... [Sighs] My very best dog, to say nothing of the expense. I gave Mironov 125 roubles for him.

cases.sentence: Позвольте, Наталья Степановна, но ведь вы забываете, что он подуздоват, а ___ всегда непоимиста!
cases.explain: «подуздоватая собака» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. Excuse me, Natalya Stepanovna, but you forget that he is overshot, and an overshot always means the dog is a bad hunter!

cases.sentence: Четвертная — ___.
cases.explain: «красная цена» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. He is old, but I wouldn't take five Squeezers for him.... Why, how can you?... Guess is a dog; as for Squeezer, well, it's too funny to argue.... Anybody you like has a dog as good as Squeezer... you may find them under every bush almost. Twenty-five roubles would be a handsome price to pay for him.

cases.sentence: Ваш Угадай, вот именно, имеет свои ___…
cases.explain: «хорошие качества» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Don't excite yourself, my precious one.... Allow me.... Your Guess certainly has his good points.... He's pure-bred, firm on his feet, has well-sprung ribs, and all that. But, my dear man, if you want to know the truth, that dog has two defects: he's old and he's short in the muzzle.

cases.sentence: Но у этой собаки, если хотите знать, красавец мой, два существенных недостатка: стара и с ___.
cases.explain: «коротким щипцом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Don't excite yourself, my precious one.... Allow me.... Your Guess certainly has his good points.... He's pure-bred, firm on his feet, has well-sprung ribs, and all that. But, my dear man, if you want to know the truth, that dog has two defects: he's old and he's short in the muzzle.

cases.sentence: Отстал, потому что ___ ударил его арапником.
cases.explain: «графский доезжачий» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. He got left behind because the Count's whipper-in hit him with his whip.

cases.sentence: Добро бы охотились, а то ведь ездите только за тем, чтобы спорить да ___ мешать и прочее.
cases.explain: «чужим собакам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Yes really, what sort of a hunter are you, anyway? You ought to sit at home with your palpitations, and not go tracking animals. You could go hunting, but you only go to argue with people and interfere with their dogs and so on. Let's change the subject in case I lose my temper. You're not a hunter at all, anyway!

cases.sentence: Замолчи, а то я подстрелю тебя из ___, как куропатку!
cases.explain: «поганого ружья» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Shut up or I'll shoot you like a partridge! You fool!

cases.sentence: — ваша ___ вас била…
cases.explain: «покойная жена» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: LOMOV. Everybody knows that--oh my heart!--your late wife used to beat you.... My feet... temples... sparks.... I fall, I fall!

cases.sentence: (Поглядев на Ломова.) В ___ помер!
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: CHUBUKOV. Who's dead? [Looks at LOMOV] So he is! My word! Water! A doctor! [Lifts a tumbler to LOMOV'S mouth] Drink this!... No, he doesn't drink.... It means he's dead, and all that.... I'm the most unhappy of men! Why don't I put a bullet into my brain? Why haven't I cut my throat yet? What am I waiting for? Give me a knife! Give me a pistol! [LOMOV moves] He seems to be coming round.... Drink some water! That's right....
